message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type (e.g., 55 mph on rural interstates, 45 mph on urban interstates).
• “No Speed Limit” zones exist on some rural highways; drivers must drive at a safe speed. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – *Speed Limits* page | | **Seat Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in tall must use a child safety seat. | TxDOT – *Seat Belt and Child Restraint* | | **DUI / Alcohol** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02%).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – *DUI* | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | TxDOT – *Distracted Driving* | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• Yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.
• In a four‑way stop, the first vehicle to arrive has the right of way. | TxDOT – *Right‑of‑Way Rules* | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Use turn signals at least 100 ft before turning. | TxDOT – *Lane Discipline* | | **School Bus** | • Stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• Do not pass a stopped school bus until it resumes motion. | TxDOT – *School Bus Rules* | | **Parking** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant.
• No parking on sidewalks or in crosswalks. | TxDOT – *Parking Regulations* | | **Vehicle Inspection** | • Annual vehicle inspection required for most vehicles.
• Inspection includes brakes, lights, tires, and emissions. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – *Vehicle Inspection* | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 bodily injury per person, $60,000 total bodily injury, $25,000 property damage. | Texas Insurance Commission – *Auto Insurance* | | **Special Situations** | • **Towing**: Must have a tow bar or chain; cannot tow a vehicle that is not in motion.
• **Emergency Vehicles**: Must yield to police, ambulance, and fire trucks. | TxDOT – *Special Vehicle Rules* | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary legal source for all traffic laws. 2. **TxDOT Website** – Offers up‑to‑date rules, safety campaigns, and downloadable handbooks. 3. **Texas DMV** – Provides licensing requirements, renewal notices, and driver education resources. 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific traffic citations or court procedures. --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety, not convenience. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or listen to music. - **Keep your vehicle in good condition** – regular inspections help avoid accidents. - **Stay alert for pedestrians and cyclists**, especially in urban areas. - **Know the local rules** – some cities have stricter regulations (e.g., no‑stop zones, bike lanes). --- #### Useful Links - [TxDOT – Traffic Safety](https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html) - [TxDOT – Vehicle Inspection](https://www.txdot.gov/vehicle-inspection.html) - [Texas DMV – Driver Licensing](https://www.txdmv.gov/) - [Texas Insurance Commission – Auto Insurance](https://www.txcic.gov/auto-insurance) Feel free to let me know if you’d like more detailed information on any specific area!
